routes.purpose: List bound sessions (device shows at most 12)
ASR for a held PTT recording
Submit a prompt and stream its run
Backfill a transcript not rendered yet
Answer a pending form ask with the chosen option value

v2_migration.tenant_boundary: ?directory= is the only tenant boundary; the client-side directory equality filter is gone
upstream_changes: all upstream paths moved under /api and responses are wrapped in {data}
POST /session/{id}/prompt_async became POST /api/session/{id}/prompt with an explicit delivery
permission, form (question), interrupt and message-history endpoints are new in v2
the v1 event vocabulary is gone: v2 splits session input, text and reasoning into separate event families
device_visible_breaking_changes: agent.reasoning.delta and agent.reasoning are new device events (reasoning never enters agent.text)
agent.question is a new device event carrying at most two projected options
GET /agent/sessions/{id}/history is a new device route; it must fit the 16 KiB JSON ceiling, so the gateway trims from the front
POST /agent/sessions/{id}/question and POST /agent/sessions/{id}/interrupt are new device routes

additive_fields.agent.tool.call_id: upstream call id echoed on every frame of one call, so two calls of the same tool are two blocks rather than one; absent only on a mid-run attach, where the device merges by tool name
additive_fields.agent.error.fatal: false marks a retryable upstream step failure: the device records the error and keeps running. Absent or true means the run is over, which is what every gateway that predates the field sends
additive_fields.agent.permission.session_id and agent.qu: the session that raised the ask, which is not always the session the device attached to: a subagent has its own id and raises its asks against it. Required, because both reply routes are session-scoped upstream -- without it a subagent's ask is discoverable but never answerable (the reply 404s on the attached session). The device still tolerates an absent field and answers on the attached session, which is what a relay that predates it wants

ask_attribution.why: the relay watches the attached session and every child of it, so an ask can arrive for a session the device never attached to
ask_attribution.device_rule: answer on the session the ask names; fall back to the attached session only when the field is absent or is not a session id
ask_attribution.gateway_rule: emit the session that actually raised the ask, never the attached one. assertOpenCodeSessionAccess accepts a child of an owned root session for the same reason
